questions.fact: Germany's consumer federation (VZBV) sued Meta and Luxottica in late November, arguing buyers weren't told data-protection law restricts filming in public and that Meta implies every feature can be used without limits. It's a court case about what buyers are told — no ban is in force and glasses are still on sale.
options: Yes — it's a lawsuit about disclosure and data protection, not a ban; sales continue
No — Germany banned all Meta glasses sales in Europe
Only Gen 3 — Gen 2 sales are paused
questions.q: A customer heard Germany is suing Meta over the smart glasses. Can they still buy a pair?

questions.fact: Snap's Specs started shipping Nov 26 to preorder customers in the US, UK and France, at $2,195 with a 51-degree field of view and the whole computer in the frame. New orders ship in early 2027 — versus the Display at $799, it's developer/early-adopter territory, not a mainstream rival.
options: Shipping to preorder customers since Nov 26; $2,195, whole computer in the frame, new orders early 2027
Out now at $799, same price as the Display
questions.q: A customer asks about Snap Specs — are they out, and how do they compare to the Display?

questions.fact: The HTC Vive Eagle launched Sep 3 at $499 and is $349.99 at HTC's store and Amazon in the Black Friday sale. It's a camera-and-audio pair in the Ray-Ban Meta mould — 12MP camera, four mics, open-ear speakers — with a $49 clip-on Power Boost battery. XREAL One Pro is a tethered display, not a camera pair, and Apple's glasses aren't out yet.
options: HTC Vive Eagle — $499 list, $349.99 in the Black Friday sale, 12MP camera and open-ear audio
XREAL One Pro at $499 — it has a camera and works standalone
Apple's smart glasses — $449, in stores now
questions.q: A customer wants camera glasses but not Meta. What's the credible alternative, and what does it cost right now?

questions.fact: Announced at Connect Sep 23, Meta VR Glasses are due spring 2027 at $1,299.99. They're a VR headset in a glasses-like frame — about 100 grams on the face, running the same apps as Quest 3 from a compute puck, with passthrough video rather than see-through lenses. Not the same category as the Display.
options: A $1,299.99 VR headset in a glasses-like frame, due spring 2027, running Quest apps from a compute puck
See-through AR glasses with a display, $799, out now
